question: A 35-year-old African American man presents with fever, abdominal pain, and severe weakness since yesterday. On physical examination, the patient is jaundiced and shows a generalized pallor. Past medical history is significant for recently receiving anti-malaria prophylaxis before visiting Nigeria. Laboratory tests show normal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) levels. Peripheral smear shows the presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fever, abdominal pain, severe weakness" -> "Possible systemic infection or inflammation" -> "Jaundice and generalized pallor" -> "Indicates liver involvement or hemolysis" -> "Bite cells and Heinz bodies in peripheral smear" -> "Indicates oxidative stress to red blood cells" -> "Normal G6PD levels" -> "G6PD deficiency less likely despite symptoms" -> "Recent anti-malaria prophylaxis" -> "Possible drug-induced hemolysis in G6PD-normal individuals" -> "Glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Fever, abdominal pain, severe weakness" -> "Signs of systemic illness" -> "Jaundice and generalized pallor" -> "Suggests hemolytic process" -> "Bite cells and Heinz bodies present" -> "Typically seen in oxidative damage to red blood cells" -> "Normal G6PD levels" -> "Rules out typical G6PD deficiency" -> "Recent travel to Nigeria with anti-malaria prophylaxis" -> "Potential exposure to oxidant drugs causing hemolysis even with normal G6PD" -> "Glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Fever, abdominal pain, severe weakness" -> "Symptoms of an acute illness" -> "Jaundice and generalized pallor" -> "Evidence of hemolysis or liver dysfunction" -> "Presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies" -> "Indicative of oxidative hemolysis" -> "Normal G6PD levels" -> "Typical G6PD deficiency unlikely but not ruled out" -> "Prophylaxis before visiting Nigeria" -> "Possible reaction to oxidative drugs used in prophylaxis" -> "Glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency" -> 65%

CHAIN: "Fever, abdominal pain, severe weakness" -> "General signs of illness" -> "Jaundice and generalized pallor" -> "Signs of anemia and possible liver involvement" -> "Bite cells and Heinz bodies in smear" -> "Associated with oxidative stress to red blood cells" -> "Normal G6PD levels" -> "G6PD deficiency usually shows decreased levels" -> "Received anti-malaria prophylaxis" -> "Drugs may induce hemolysis even in normal G6PD levels" -> "Glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings suggest a hemolytic anemia, characterized by jaundice, pallor, and the presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies in the peripheral smear. Bite cells and Heinz bodies are typically associated with oxidative stress to red blood cells, commonly seen in G6PD deficiency. Despite the normal G6PD levels reported, these can be intermittently normal in G6PD deficiency, especially if the test is not performed during an acute hemolytic episode. The recent use of anti-malaria prophylaxis, which can include drugs known to precipitate hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals, supports this diagnosis.
